The regression was in `sqlparse/filters/aligned_indent.py` in `_process_case`. The list comprehension computing `condition_width` had its ternary branches swapped:

```python
condition_width = [0 if cond else len(' '.join(map(str, cond)))
                   for cond, _ in cases]
```

When `cond` was falsy (i.e. `None`, representing the ELSE/END entries), it incorrectly tried `map(str, cond)` on `None`, raising `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable`. When `cond` was truthy (an actual list of condition tokens) it just returned 0, losing the real width entirely.

Fixed by swapping the branches so the width is computed only when a condition exists, and 0 otherwise:

```python
condition_width = [len(' '.join(map(str, cond))) if cond else 0
                   for cond, _ in cases]
```

Verified manually that both a plain CASE/WHEN/ELSE statement and one using BETWEEN now format correctly with `reindent_aligned=True`, producing properly aligned WHEN/ELSE/END clauses without raising an exception. No local test suite directory exists in this checkout (only the `sqlparse` package itself), so hidden upstream tests will be used for final verification.
